title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for history of prostate cancer.

HPI
Pt is a 76-year-old male presenting for surveillance of prostate carcinoma. Pt had the primary cancer removed and treated years ago. Treatment is complete. Pt reports feeling well and denies any new urinary symptoms or pelvic pain. He notes no changes in bowel or bladder habits.

Medication List
Multivitamin daily
Lisinopril 10mg daily

Exam
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 72, RR 16, Temp 98.6F.
Respiratory: CTAB, RRR.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no masses.
Genitourinary: No complaints of dysuria.

Assessment
1. History of prostate cancer. Primary site shows no evidence of local recurrence. No evidence of disease elsewhere. Treatment complete.

Plan
1. Continue surveillance. No active treatment indicated at this time. Pt to return in 6 months for routine follow-up.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
05/14/2026
explanations: The prostate cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.46 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
